Maya (support): :rotating_light: Customer Acorn hitting severe p99/p95 spikes during billing window (17:10-17:30 UTC). They report p99 ~6s, lots of 503/504 attach timeouts and intermittent 401 auth failures. They say traffic spiked ~20k qps for ~2m. Pool: acorn-prod-pool (Dedicated). Ticket #AC-12345. Posting sample logs below.

Kevin (oncall): Can you paste the basic repro steps + a couple request_ids? I'll start looking at the autoscale metrics.

Maya (support): Repro: hit the same load generator they ran (link) — we saw attach backlog. Sample request ids: req_20260317_01, req_20260317_02. Logs:
```
[17:12:03] req_20260317_01 ERR_ATTACH_TIMEOUT attach_id=attach-7f3 auth=200->401 handshake=timeout
[17:12:04] req_20260317_02 ERR_ATTACH_TIMEOUT attach_id=attach-8a1 image_pull=slow auth=401
[17:12:05] req_20260317_03 503 Provisioner busy queue_len=842
```

Ravi (eng-sre): Looking at infra: attach queue length spiked to ~1200 at 17:12, attach success rate dropped, and many nodes stuck in ContainerCreating. Kernel image pull latencies to our registry jumped from 200ms->3s (likely registry throttling). Also acorn-prod-pool had min_replicas=0 so warm capacity was zero when the burst hit. Autoscaler did scale but attach handshake + image pull made effective scaleup slow.

Ravi (eng-sre): Immediate mitigations I'd run now:
- bump min for pool to keep warm GPUs: `rictl pool update acorn-prod-pool --min 2`
- enable fallback route for Acorn to hosted (if customer allows): `rictl routing set acorn --fallback hosted`
- temporarily increase attach timeouts and backoff to avoid thundering herd: `rictl flags set attach_backoff_ms=2000 attach_timeout_ms=45000`
- prime images on nodes / pre-pull kernel image (infra job): `kubectl -n infra run prepull --image=registry.redwood/llm-kernel:stable --replicas=2 -- /bin/true`

Nia (svc-eng): +1 to bumping min. Also suggest enabling the light-weight auth retry shim for this customer (reduces 401 noise while we probe). Command: `rictl customers set acorn --auth-retry=enabled`. Could also temporarily move them to priority queue to get allocs faster if their contract allows.

Kevin (oncall): I'll run the min bump and set fallback route. Executing now.

Support Bot: Incident created INC-20260317-ACORN-1 (auto). Notifying oncall rotation.

Kevin (oncall): Done: `rictl pool update acorn-prod-pool --min 2` -> 2 nodes requested. `rictl routing set acorn --fallback hosted` -> enabled. Started pre-pull job.

Ravi (eng-sre): Observing metrics after changes: attach queue down from 1200 -> ~150 over 90s, attach success rate climbing. Image pull lat median reduced after pre-pull. Auth 401s still sporadic but trending down after `auth-retry` toggle. p99 dropped from ~6s -> ~700ms.

Maya (support): Updated customer about mitigation and that we routed burst traffic to hosted as a temporary safety valve. Customer acknowledged, will re-run their load test in 10m and report.

Nia (svc-eng): Postmortem action items (short):
- set pool min defaults to 1 for high-SLA Dedicated pools
- add registry retry/backoff and image pre-pull in autoscale path
- refine attach handshake to be resilient to image-pull delays (defer KV cache init until attach confirmed)
- add alert for min_replicas==0 on SLA pools during billing windows

Kevin (oncall): Great. I'll keep the incident open for monitoring and escalate to eng-platform if we see a recurrence. :thumbsup:

Maya (support): Closing loop: customer will validate. Will file follow-up with timeline and logs to #support-postmortems.

Ravi (eng-sre): Filing quick RCA draft, will ping when ready.

Support Bot: Incident INC-20260317-ACORN-1 status=monitoring assigned_to=oncall

Kevin (oncall): Marking this thread resolved for now but will re-open if customer sees more p99s. :white_check_mark:
